forecaster_note: Surf Guru read: You're into the mid-morning window now on a clean winter Sunday — a solid long-period S groundswell is running (6.8ft @ 11s from 181°, ~1011 kJ) under a WSW offshore that's freshening to 28 km/h gusts and starting to add a little texture. The catch is direction: it's dead-south, which wraps soft into Dee Why and is heavily shadowed at Manly, so the size lives at the S-exposed banks — Long Reef (head to overhead, biggest of the four) and Curl Curl. Dee Why still rates fair-good off the Point where the S corners into a clean frontside right. Don't dawdle: the 11:22am low is draining the banks and the WSW is building, so this session is best in the next hour or so. Tomorrow the swell drops hard to waist-chest; a much bigger S pulse (10ft @ 10s, ~2130 kJ) is building toward late week. 🦈 SharkSmart's live detection feed is still down this refresh (server 503) — no NSW detections could be read, so check the live map before you paddle out.

swells.label: Primary S groundswell — wraps soft here

dee-why.window: The Point is the play — a wrapping dead-S holds a clean frontside right while the open beach stays shadowed. 1011 kJ at 11s is real groundswell but feeds Dee Why side-on. Best in the next hour: the WSW is freshening and the 11:22am low is draining it.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: Dead-S 181° wraps weak into the beach, so set up wide on the Point where it corners into a rippable right. WSW offshore and an 11s period — pick the sets and drive off the bottom turn. Shape over raw size here.

long-reef.window: Standout for size — the S-swell magnet turns 181° into head-to-overhead sets. WSW is close to straight offshore here, so it's the cleanest of the four; go now before the gusts build.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: This is where the size lives — overhead sets off a solid 11s S groundswell. 1011 kJ has real push, so take off deep and it'll run. Step toward the FMN3 if the sets stack up.

curl-curl.window: Second for size behind Long Reef — punchy chest-to-head-high off cleaner banks. Grab it now under the WSW offshore before the low drains it.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: More exposed than Dee Why so it grabs the S swell — hunt the banked lefts on your backhand and stay high through the fatter sections. Clean offshore, just freshening.

manly.window: Smallest and most protected — thigh-to-chest, clean under the WSW offshore but well under what the other three are doing. Not worth the drive over Long Reef today.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: North Steyne stays small on a dead-S swell — soft, forgiving corners. Groveller if you just want easy water time; otherwise chase the size up at Long Reef.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Swell drops hard — waist-to-chest S leftovers (4.4ft @ 9s, ~236 kJ) on a light ENE breeze that nudges onshore. Long Reef holds the most size and cleanest rating. A low-key day; save yourself for the big S pulse building toward late week.

dee-why.window: Much smaller and the light ENE is onshore — soft, tumbly beachbreak. The Point still offers the cleanest corner. Dawn before the sea breeze fills in.

long-reef.window: Best of the four again — holds the most size and the ENE is more cross-side here. Early is cleanest before the breeze swings onshore.

curl-curl.window: Small and soft on the light onshore — grab it early or wait for the weekend pulse.

manly.window: Tiny — a longboard or groveller session at best.

days.label: Weekend

Big and powerful — the S-exposed banks (Long Reef, Curl Curl) could push well overhead, Dee Why holds a clean fair-good right off the Point, Manly stays shadowed. Re-check midweek once the forecast window opens up.

alerts: Early read — forecast doesn't reach next weekend yet; based on the Fri 31 Jul projection. Big-but-dead-S energy wraps soft into Dee Why; the Point grooms it into a clean right.
dee-why.window: The Point is the pick on a big S — a long, clean frontside right while the beachies stay shadowed. Shape over size; step-up board.

long-reef.window: Biggest of the run by far — solid overhead-plus sets at the S magnet. SW adds some bump; earliest is cleanest. Step-up board and respect it — the serious session.

curl-curl.window: Well overhead and punchy — handles the big S far better than Dee Why. Go early before the wind.

alerts: Even a big S is heavily shadowed by the southern headland — smallest of the four by a wide margin, but the cleanest and most manageable option.
manly.window: Clean but shadowed — the manageable pick if the bigger banks are too much.
